Sampled HR@10 with 99 negatives measures performance under that candidate protocol; model rankings can differ from full-catalog rankings, even in expectation. Keep the pinned evaluator unchanged and interpret gains within its scope. Fixed seeds support reproducible comparisons but do not establish robustness across training randomness or candidate samples. [Krichene and Rendle, 2020](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

For this benchmark, a defensible diagnostic is a paired, category-stratified user bootstrap: retain each model’s binary hit for every validation user, resample the same user indices for both models within each category, then average the four category differences with equal weight. Report the macro difference, its bootstrap interval, and category scores. With 200 users/category, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fixed models and candidate sets; they exclude training-seed variation and search-selection bias. Bootstrap and randomization methods have supporting evidence in recommendation evaluation, though the cited study emphasizes large samples. [Ihemelandu and Ekstrand, 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.02461).

Repeatedly selecting architectures or checkpoints on the same small validation set risks overfitting the selection criterion; an ordinary bootstrap interval does not remove that optimism. Practical implication: predefine checkpoint frequency, selection and tie rules, and a bounded search within 43,200 GPU-seconds; log every trial and checkpoint comparison. Select by the required macro validation HR@10, treating uncertainty as supporting evidence rather than replacing the objective. Reserve claims about generalization for the independent held-out evaluation. [Cawley and Talbot, 2010](https://jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html).
